1. Purpose

1.1 This Standard sets the mandatory requirements for the secure
configuration of technology assets, the management of technical
vulnerabilities, the application of patches, the treatment of unsupported
technology, and the control of change. It is the sole authoritative source
in this corpus for configuration baselines, vulnerability remediation
timelines and change control requirements.

1.2 This Standard gives effect to the secure-by-design-and-by-default
principle at [MDS-CS-POL-001 §7.5] and the deny-by-default principle at
[§7.3].

2. Scope

2.1 This Standard applies to every technology asset in the Company
estate, including: servers, workstations, laptops and mobile devices;
network and security appliances; hypervisors and container platforms;
databases, middleware and message brokers; operating systems and
their components; cloud resources and managed services; container
images; infrastructure-as-code definitions; and the operational
technology in scope of [MDS-CS-POL-002 §13], subject to §13.6 of that
Manual.

2.2 The Standard applies in all environments. Non-production
environments are in scope; a lower baseline is not permitted merely
because an environment is non-production, although §7.2 sets different
remediation timelines by environment.

3. Definitions

3.1 Terms have the meanings at [MDS-CS-REF-001], in particular:
baseline, golden image, configuration drift, authenticated scan, actively

exploited vulnerability, and emergency change.

4. Roles

4.1 The Head of Cybersecurity Engineering owns this Standard and
approves every baseline.

4.2 The technical custodian of an asset, as recorded under [MDS-CS-
POL-002 §4.2], is accountable for applying the baseline, remediating
vulnerabilities within the timelines at §7.2, and maintaining the asset
within vendor support.

4.3 The business information asset owner is accountable for
accepting any residual risk arising from a deviation, through the
exception process at [MDS-CS-POL-001 §10].

5. Configuration Baselines

5.1 Every asset type in the Company estate shall have a documented,
approved configuration baseline. An asset shall not be deployed into any
environment before a baseline exists for its type and has been applied.

5.2 Baselines shall be derived from a recognised secure configuration
benchmark — Center for Internet Security Benchmarks at Level 1 as a
minimum, or the vendor's published security configuration guidance
where no benchmark exists — and shall then be adjusted for the
Company environment. Every deviation from the source benchmark
shall be documented with its justification in the baseline document itself.

5.3 Baselines shall be approved by the Head of Cybersecurity
Engineering before use, and shall be version-controlled with a
documented change history.

5.4 Baselines shall be reviewed at intervals not exceeding twelve (12)
months, and additionally within sixty (60) calendar days of the

publication of a new major version of the source benchmark or of the
underlying product.

5. Configuration Baselines
5.5 Every baseline shall address, as a minimum: removal or disabling of
unnecessary services, protocols, daemons, roles, features and sample
content; closure of unnecessary network ports; removal or disabling of
default and guest accounts and change of default credentials per [MDS-
CS-STD-001 §8.6]; the minimum authentication configuration required
by [MDS-CS-STD-001]; the cryptographic configuration required by
[MDS-CS-STD-002], including approved protocol versions and cipher
suites; the audit logging configuration required by [MDS-CS-STD-004

§5]; time synchronisation per [MDS-CS-STD-004 §8]; host firewall
configuration; malicious code protection per §10; secure boot and
firmware protection where supported; file integrity monitoring on systems
in criticality Tier 1; and the administrative access restrictions at [MDS-
CS-STD-001 §7].

5.6 Privileged access workstations shall be built to a dedicated
hardened baseline that additionally: removes email, instant messaging
and general web browsing capability; permits outbound network
connections only to a defined list of management endpoints; enforces
application allow-listing in default-deny mode; prohibits removable media
entirely; requires AAL-3 authentication at logon per [MDS-CS-STD-001

§5.3.1]; prohibits the workstation being used for any non-administrative
task; and is rebuilt from the golden image at intervals not exceeding one
hundred and eighty (180) calendar days.

§5]; time synchronisation per [MDS-CS-STD-004 §8]; host firewall
5.7 Systems shall be built from an approved golden image where one
exists. Golden images shall be rebuilt and re-hardened at intervals not
exceeding thirty (30) calendar days so that newly deployed systems
are not deployed already requiring patches, and shall be scanned for
vulnerabilities before release.

5.8 Infrastructure defined as code shall have its definitions stored in
version control, peer-reviewed before merge per [MDS-CS-STD-006

§5.4], and scanned automatically for insecure configuration before
deployment. Manual changes to infrastructure that is managed as code
are prohibited outside an emergency change under §9.6, and shall be
reconciled back into code within five (5) business days.

5.9 Container images shall be built from an approved minimal base
image, shall not run as root, shall not include a shell or package
manager in the production image where the runtime permits, and shall
be scanned per [MDS-CS-STD-006 §8.4] before being admitted to a
production registry.

6. Configuration Compliance and Drift

6.1 Compliance with the applicable baseline shall be measured
automatically for every asset at intervals not exceeding twenty-four (24)
hours, and results shall be reported to the platform required by [MDS-
CS-STD-004].

6.2 Configuration drift from an approved baseline shall be alerted to the
technical custodian and shall be remediated within: seven (7) calendar
days for a setting classified in the baseline as security-critical; thirty
(30) calendar days otherwise. Drift on a system in criticality Tier 1 that
affects a security-critical setting shall additionally raise an alert per
[MDS-CS-STD-004 §7.2].

6.3 An asset shall not be admitted to a production network until it
evidences baseline compliance. Assets found in production without an
applied baseline shall be treated as an incident under [MDS-CS-
POL-001 §8].

6.4 Baseline compliance percentage by asset class shall be reported
monthly to the Cybersecurity Operations Forum and quarterly to the
Cybersecurity Committee, using the metric at [MDS-CS-REF-003 Annex
G].

7.1.2 External attack surface discovery shall run continuously and shall
reconcile discovered internet-facing assets against the inventory

7.1.3 Scanning shall be authenticated wherever technically possible. An
unauthenticated scan shall not be reported as evidence of the absence
of vulnerabilities.

7. Vulnerability and Patch Management
7.1.4 Assets that cannot be scanned by the standard tooling — including
certain operational technology in scope of [MDS-CS-POL-002 §13] —
shall be assessed by an alternative method, such as passive network

7. Vulnerability and Patch Management
7.2.2 The base score shall be adjusted using environmental and
temporal metrics where the Company's context materially changes the
risk. An adjustment that lowers a severity shall be documented, shall
state the compensating factor relied upon, and shall be approved by the
Head of Cybersecurity Engineering. An adjustment that raises a severity
requires no approval and takes effect immediately.

7.2.3 Where a vendor patch is not available within the applicable period,
the technical custodian shall implement a documented mitigation —
configuration change, virtual patching at the network or application layer,
service disablement, or isolation — within the same period, and shall
raise an exception per [MDS-CS-POL-001 §10] for the residual exposure
until the patch is applied.

7.3 Prioritisation and exploitation

7. Vulnerability and Patch Management
7.3.1 Where a vulnerability is subject to active exploitation —
evidenced by an advisory of the National Cybersecurity Authority, a
recognised known-exploited-vulnerability catalogue, credible threat
intelligence assessed under [MDS-CS-POL-002 §10.12], or observation
within the Company estate — the timelines at §7.2.1 do not apply and

§7.4 applies instead, irrespective of the CVSS score.

7.3.2 A vulnerability with a working public exploit but no evidence of
active exploitation shall be treated as one severity level higher than its
base score for the purpose of §7.2.1.

7.4 Emergency response to actively exploited
vulnerabilities

7.4.3 Where the applicable period cannot be met, the affected service

7.4.4 The CISO may direct the immediate isolation of any asset
presenting an imminent threat, without prior change approval and
without the consent of the asset owner.

7.5 Reporting

7.5.1 Open vulnerabilities past their §7.2.1 or §7.4.1 due date shall be
reported weekly to the technical custodian's line management, monthly
to the Cybersecurity Operations Forum, and quarterly to the
Cybersecurity Committee, using the metric at [MDS-CS-REF-003 Annex
G].

7.5.2 Findings from penetration testing under [MDS-CS-POL-001 §9.2]
shall be entered into the same remediation workflow, with severity
mapped to the scale at §7.2.1, and shall be closed on the evidence
standard at [MDS-CS-POL-001 §9.6].

8. Unsupported and End-of-Life Technology

8.1 Technology that has reached the end of vendor security support
shall not be operated in any Company environment. Its removal or
upgrade shall be planned at least twelve (12) months before the
published end-of-support date.

8.2 The Company shall maintain a forward register of end-of-support
dates for all products in the estate, reviewed quarterly, and shall report
to the Cybersecurity Committee any product reaching end of support
within the next twelve months without a funded replacement plan.

8.3 Where continued operation is unavoidable, an exception shall be
approved under [MDS-CS-POL-001 §10] at the authority level
corresponding to the residual risk, and shall implement all of the

following compensating controls, each with a named owner:

• 8.3.1 network isolation of the asset into a dedicated segment with
an explicit, minimal allow-list of permitted flows;

• 8.3.2 removal of all direct user access, with access mediated
through a broker or jump host under [MDS-CS-STD-001 §7.4];

following compensating controls, each with a named owner:
• 8.3.3 enhanced monitoring, with the asset's events treated as
high-fidelity and alerted on per [MDS-CS-STD-004 §7.2];

• 8.3.4 application allow-listing in default-deny mode on the asset
where the platform supports it;

• 8.3.5 virtual patching at the network or application layer for known
vulnerabilities affecting it;

• 8.3.6 a documented, funded migration plan with dates, reported to
the Cybersecurity Committee at each quarterly meeting until the
asset is decommissioned; and

• 8.3.7 where the asset is internet-facing, its withdrawal from
internet exposure — an internet-facing unsupported asset shall
not be permitted to remain internet-facing under any exception.

8.4 Extended security support purchased from the vendor satisfies §8.1
for the duration of that support, provided it includes security patches for
the vulnerabilities in scope of §7.

9. Change Management

9.1 Every change to a production system, network, security control or
cloud configuration shall be recorded, assessed, authorised,
implemented and reviewed through the Company change management
process. Undocumented change to production is prohibited.

9.2 A change record shall state: the change description and its purpose;
the systems and services affected; the assessed risk, including its
cybersecurity impact; the implementation plan; the test evidence; the
back-out plan; the verification steps; and the named implementer and
approver.

9.3 Changes shall be classified as standard (pre-approved, low-risk,

repeatable, executed from a documented procedure), normal (requiring
Change Advisory Board authorisation), or emergency (§9.6).

9.4 Every normal change shall be assessed for cybersecurity impact
before authorisation. A change assessed as having a cybersecurity
impact shall not proceed without the approval of the Cybersecurity
representative on the Change Advisory Board, who holds a veto per
[MDS-CS-POL-001 §5.3].

9. Change Management
9.5 Changes shall be tested in a non-production environment
representative of production before implementation. The person who
implements a change into production shall not be the sole person who
approved it, per the segregation principle at [MDS-CS-POL-001 §7.2].

9.6 Emergency change. An emergency change may be implemented
without prior Change Advisory Board authorisation where delay would
cause a service outage, a security compromise, or a breach of the
timelines at §7.4. It shall be authorised at the time by the on-call senior
manager of the affected platform and the CISO or a delegate for any
security-affecting change; shall be recorded in the change system
within four (4) hours of implementation; and shall be reviewed at the
next Change Advisory Board meeting, which shall assess whether the
emergency route was justified.

9.7 A change freeze shall apply during periods of elevated business risk
as published by IT Service Management. Changes during a freeze
require executive authorisation, except emergency changes under §9.6.

9. Change Management
9.8 Post-implementation verification shall confirm that the change
achieved its purpose and that security controls — logging,
authentication, encryption, monitoring agents — remain in place and
functioning. Where a change disables a security control temporarily, its
restoration shall be verified explicitly and recorded.

9.9 Unauthorised change detected by configuration monitoring under §6
shall be investigated as a potential incident under [MDS-CS-POL-001

§8] and shall not be retrospectively legitimised by raising a change
record after the fact.

10. Malicious Code Protection

10.1 Malicious code protection shall be deployed on all servers,
endpoints, email gateways, web gateways and file transfer points, and
shall be configured to update signatures and detection content
automatically at intervals not exceeding four (4) hours.

10.2 Protection shall include behavioural and heuristic detection in
addition to signature matching, and shall be integrated with the detection
platform required by [MDS-CS-STD-004].

10.3 Scanning exclusions shall be approved by the Head of
Cybersecurity Engineering, shall be as narrow as possible, shall be
documented with justification, and shall be reviewed at intervals not
exceeding one hundred and eighty (180) calendar days. Exclusion of
an entire drive, an entire file type, or a user-writable directory tree is
prohibited.

§8] and shall not be retrospectively legitimised by raising a change
10.4 Email attachments and downloaded files of types capable of
carrying executable content shall be detonated in a sandbox before
delivery, and macros in files originating from outside the Company shall
be blocked by policy.

10.5 Detection of malicious code shall be treated as a cybersecurity
incident and reported per [MDS-CS-POL-001 §8.2], whether or not the
protection reports successful remediation.

11. Compliance, Exceptions and Related
Documents

11.1 Compliance shall be measured by the automated mechanisms at

§6.1 and §7.1 and reported per §6.4 and §7.5.1.

11.2 Exceptions shall be handled per [MDS-CS-POL-001 §10], and
unsupported technology exceptions additionally per §8.3.

11.3 Related documents: [MDS-CS-POL-001 §7.5], §9.2, §10; [MDS-
